key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of perovskites from accelerated ageing data, generalizing to unseen samples and material groups.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, lower-cost stability screening for perovskite solar materials by reducing the need for long experimental ageing tests.
method: Collected 167 metal halide perovskite samples with varied compositions and crystallinities under heat/light stress.
Converted more than 86k PL spectra into physics-informed features for model input.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity and identify stability descriptors with explainability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a diverse dataset of 167 samples and over 86k PL spectra, with the model outperforming baseline benchmarks on unseen samples.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the stress conditions and spectra, so deployment on new chemistries or protocols should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
